articleTitle: A Simple I-Shaped Wideband Linear-Linear and Linear-Circular Reflective Type Polarizer
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A wideband angular stable linear-cross and linear-circular reflective type polarization converter has been illustrated in this work. The unitcell comprises a 45° rotated circular-arc based I-shaped resonator printed on top of a thin FR-4 grounded dielectric substrate. The proposed metasurface converts y/x- polarized incidence wave to its cross-polarization in three different frequency ranges: C, X, and Ku-bands. This design can also convert linearly polarized wave into circular polarization in C and Ku-bands along with linear-orthogonal conversion. The response is stable up to 45° (for linear-cross) and 30° (linear-circular) for both oblique incidences (TE and TM). The uniqueness of the design lies in dual-polarization conversion in the same bands and cell compactness with periodicity 0.1539 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>, and 0.0535 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> (λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> refers to the longest free-space wavelength of the operational band). Authors strongly believe this design has the potential to be used in real-time application where the dual-polarization conversion (linear as well circular) has the primary need.

articleTitle: Broadband Single Layer Transmission Type Linear to Circular Polarization Converter with Higher Conversion Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents a broadband transmission type linear to circular polarization converter (LCPC) with the advantages of a single metal layer, high conversion efficiency, and low insertion loss (IL). The proposed unit cell consists of narrow and wide metal strips which are oriented along the two diagonals. The strips exhibit high pass filtering characteristics with low cutoff frequency and higher resonance outside the operational band. The two orthogonal transmitted components from the metasurface have approximately equal magnitudes with a phase difference of 90° and the resultant wave is right-hand circular polarized (RCP). The proposed converter shows a 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) of 48.2 % between 19.22-31.42 GHz. The unit cell has a periodicity of 2.4 mm or 0.2 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the wavelength at the center frequency of the operational bandwidth (BW). The proposed structure shows incidence angle stability up to 35° in two principal planes.

articleTitle: High Gain Low-Cost 20 GHz Antenna Design Based on the Utilization of Diffracted Fields from Dielectric Edges
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: We propose a low cost antenna solution, the antenna has 21-dBi gain. A thorough analysis of the propagation mechanism accompanied by a unique physical insight is presented. The realized structure has a low profile, low cost, and compact size features.

articleTitle: Parasitic-Based Electrically Small CLL Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Based on near-field coupling design strategy, an electrically small antenna is presented. The antenna is composed of a driven element fed differentially, and a parasitic capacitive loaded loop. The parasitic based antenna is printed on an RF substrate and has a maximum dimension of 28.80 mm, electrical size ka=0.261, designed to resonate at 868 MHz. The antenna is optimized with CST-MWS to realize maximum possible radiation efficiency where predictions shows nearly 76% for lossless loading capacitor and 69% for a lossy capacitor. A complete impedance matching is directly obtained by acting on the antenna geometry resulting in a proper near field coupling between driven element and parasitic element.

articleTitle: Passenger Monitoring Using AI-Powered Radar
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Low-cost, contactless and privacy-preserving radar-based sensors are gaining attention for in-vehicle passenger monitoring. In this paper, we address two major topics in in-vehicle occupancy detection using radar technologies: 1. Detection of any living body left alone in a car. 2. Passenger counting. For the first one, we propose a novel, easy-to-implement and fast radar signal processing algorithm to detect the presence of alive subjects (e.g., infants, kids, pets), which is 100% accurate in detecting any tiny subject. For the latter one, we address radar low-resolution problems and propose machine learning to be coupled with radar signal processing to count the number of occupants and identify their occupied seats. Our proposed in-vehicle occupancy detection reaches more than 90% accuracy for each seat.

articleTitle: Single Channel mmWave FMCW Radar for 2D Target Localization
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, we present a 2D target localization method using two low cost and compact Mellimeter Wave Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (MMW-FMCW) radars. To create a 2D map we exploit the bilateration method followed by a multi-target tracking block to remove the ghost targets. Finally, we present experimental results based on the data gathered from two FMCW radars operating at 79 GHz.

articleTitle: Capacitively Coupled Single-Layer Dual-Band Circularly Polarized GPS Ring Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A low profile, capacitively coupled circularly polarized dual-band Global Positioning System (GPS) antenna with orthogonal dual feed is simulated and presented. The antenna is designed to operate at the GPS L1 (1575.42 MHz) and L2 (1227.60 MHz) frequencies. Geometric parameters are varied to test the effect on the operating frequencies, axial ratio, and radiation pattern. A bandwidth of 7 MHz at L1 and 5 MHz at L2 was achieved. The 3 dB axial ratio beamwidth was 72° at L1 and 180° at L2. These results were achieved with overall patch dimensions of 55.6mm X 55.6mm on a single layer.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Dual-Band 28/38 GHz Frequency Selective Surface for 6G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, a reconfigurable dual-band frequency selective surfaces (FSS) for millimeter 6G applications is presented. The proposed design can reconfigure the functional characteristics of FSS unit cell operation between the stop and pass band at 28GHz and 38GHz, respectively. The transmission/ reflection characteristics are investigated by changing the baising of the diode, where a U-shaped notch filter is deployed to achieve the rejection at 38GHz. The operation of the proposed unitcell is validated through simulation using CST software.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Improvement of Transparent Meshed Patch Antennas Using Stacking Technique
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, two squared optically transparent meshed patch antennas are stacked on top of each other to achieve the bandwidth of 3.5 times higher than the single-layer squared meshed patch antenna. Both layers are designed on glass substrate Corning 7070 to maintain transparency and integrability with solar cells. The design frequency is 2.45 GHz, and the gain variation is less than 1 dB in the entire bandwidth.

articleTitle: High Gain Circularly Polarized 30 GHz Antenna using 3D Printing Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: We propose a low cost high gain circularly polarized antenna, the proposed antenna achieves a gain of 20-dBi, and an axial ratio bandwidth of 6.5%. The proposed antenna is extremely low in cost and avoids the design of any feeding network. The antenna is well suited for narrow band mm-wave applications.

articleTitle: A New Endfire Phased Array based on Vivaldi Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper proposes a new configuration of an Endfire wide-scaning phased array antenna operating at millimeter wave at 28 GHz. The proposed antenna is considered as low-cost device designed on standard FR4 substrate with a thickness of 0.5 mm, a permittivity of 4.4, and a total size of 44 × 16 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Eight Vivaldi antenna elements fed by microstrip lines have been used to form a linear array at the top side of the cellphone PCB. The gain antenna is improved by using a periodic printed metallic strip that act as a directors. This technique achieves a large bandwith of 3 GHz from 26.5 to 29.5 GHz, and a high gain of 15 dBi which is almost stable over a wide scanning angle.

articleTitle: Dual Differential-Fed 2×2 Phased Array with Reconfigurable Polarization and Radiation Pattern Diversity
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A 2×2 phased array with simplified control of six polarization states and two sets of radiation patterns is presented. Implementing two single pole single throw switches (SPSTs) and three phase shifters results in six different polarization states, including 0°, 90°, ±45° linear polarization (LP), right-hand circular polarization (RHCP), and left-hand circular polarization (LHCP). Moreover, two types of radiation patterns, including a single main-beam at broadside and multi-beams (i.e., 4 Beams) are achieved using the proposed topologies. Configurations of monolithic microwave integrated circuits (MMICs) used in the feed network are presented. The antenna has an operating frequency band of 9.25−9.55 GHz. The peak realized gain for broadside main-beam and 4 Beams at 9.45 GHz are 12.47 dB and 6.57 dB, respectively. The radiation pattern and polarization diversity along with the compactness and relatively high gain of the proposed phase array, make it a suitable candidate for Radar and navigation systems.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave High Gain Scanning Antenna Array using Printed RGW Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, a high gain magneto-electric (ME) dipole scanning antenna array for millimeter-wave applications is presented. The antenna array is fed by a printed ridge gap waveguide (PRGW) Butler matrix to have four beams elevated at 20 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> from the broadside direction. A hybrid gain enhancement technique including AMC mushroom shapes around the antenna array with a perforated dielectric substrate lens located in the broadside direction is proposed. The proposed scanning array is achieved a high gain of 15± 1 dB over the operating bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Compact Uniplanar Electromagnetic Bandgap Structure with Wide Bandgap
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents a new compact uniplanar electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structure for K band applications. The proposed unit cell consists of corner square patches which are connected at the center by meander lines and interdigital capacitors (IDC) along the edges. The dispersion characteristic of the EBG is analyzed using an Eigenmode solver and later the bandgap property is verified using an open-ended symmetric transmission line method. Numerical simulation of the proposed EBG shows a bandgap of 21.5 % over 17.33−21.5 GHz. The unit cell has the periodicity of 0.16 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the wavelength at the center frequency of the bandgap.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network for Microwave Filter Design using a Circuit Model
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This research work utilized one of the key techniques of machine learning, artificial neural network to train and learn the relationship between the parameters of a lossless microwave filter in order to address the nonlinearity challenge of microwave filter design. Due to non-suitability of the commonly known Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) in modeling of microwave filters, a Leaky version of ReLU is utilized. A model is developed for the design of a capacitively coupled series resonator band pass filter.

articleTitle: Design of a UHF / UWB monopole antenna integrated in an RFID reader board
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this study, we present a new circular monopole antenna with triple-band characteristics that can operate in both the ultra-high frequency (UHF) and ultra-wideband (UWB) bands and is integrated into a radio frequency identification (RFID) system reader module. In fact, the antenna was equipped with a patch and a CPW feed to meet the bandwidth specifications for RFID applications at UHF/UWB. To connect with RFID tags, this antenna is manufactured and inserted into the RFID reader board. Experiments show that the UHF-RFID efficiency of the monopole antenna is comparable to that of current commercial solutions.

articleTitle: 3D Near-Field Millimeter-Wave Synthetic Aperture Radar Imaging
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, we present 3D high resolution radar imaging process at millimeter-Wave (mmWave) frequencies by creating the effect of a large aperture synthetically. We use a low cost fully integrated Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar operating at 79 GHz and then perform Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imaging in the near-filed zone.At the end, we conduct a real experiment and present the reconstructed image.

articleTitle: Design of Dual Circular Polarized Wideband Stacked Patch Flat Panel Phased Array Antenna using Ka-band 5G Silicon RFICs in Beamforming Network
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: An 8×8 dual circularly polarized phased array antenna with very low cross-polarization that covers wideband (22.5-27.5 GHz) and offers broadside circular polarized (CP) realized gain of around 22-23 dBic is proposed. The radiating element consists of a square driven patch and a square parasitic patch placed over it, with two orthogonal feed points at the driven patch. In each 2×2 subarray unit of the 8×8 array, upper right and lower left radiating elements are mirrored with respect to a vertical plane for high cross-polarization suppression. A beamforming network utilizing Anokiwave RFICs that feed four radiating elements, will be employed to achieve beam scanning. The circular polarization is obtained when 90° time-phase difference is applied between two feed points of the patch using the RFICs. A suitable beamforming algorithm will be applied through SPI controller. The circular polarized beam scans till ±46°.

articleTitle: Phase Shifting Trimmer with Small Precision Phase Change for Offsetting Process-Voltage-Temperature Tolerances
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Phase Shifters (especially the digitally-controlled ones) often tend to omit phase shifting capabilities of less than 5.625° of phase change; due to heavy insertion and return loss performance degradation every time a phase-shifting block is appended to the overall phase shifting chain. In this work, an architecture is shown how one can achieve such small changes of phase (for use as a least-significant-bit stepper); without heavy performance sacrifice. The architecture presented is a series of diode loaded transmission line phase shifter (similar to microwave delay line for analog signal correction) for trimming (or calibrating) though small phase steps. The proof-of-concept trimmer operates at 2.5 GHz and has 8-bits. It traverses a total phase change of 1.2° and it has an average phase change of 0.16° per bit (degrees/bit). For small phase changes, the return and insertion losses deliverance from this architecture might be the best available from the different types of phase shifting compositions out there (if properly designed); and can be used in conjunction with other phase shifting blocks. The trimmer in this work had return loss better than −20 dB and insertion loss of less than 1.2 dB for all 8 states.

articleTitle: C-band Backscatter of Oil-polluted New Sea Ice in a Mesocosm
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: We present an assessment of C-band scatterometer measurements of oil-polluted sea ice in the University of Manitoba’s Sea-ice Environmental Research facility (SERF) mesocosm. Oil was released beneath an established ice sheet and physical characteristics were measured throughout the experiment. Polarimetric backscatter observations of oil seepage through the ice surface show sensitivity in the backscatter intensity. These results increase our understanding of backscattering response to oil-in-sea ice, critical to early oil spill detection in the Arctic marine environment.

articleTitle: Design of Short Backfire Antennas for Remote Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, we present design, simulation, and measurements for a short backfire antenna that has been developed for remote sensing applications. The antenna is fed with a standard rectangular waveguide and operates in C-band. We performed parametric studies on the antenna geometry and determined an optimal configuration that provides a realized gain of 14.53 dBi and bandwidth of 1.19 GHz. A prototype was fabricated and test results verified the performance.

articleTitle: Initial characterization of a porTable breast microwave detection device
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Breast cancer is the most commonly diagnosed cancer and the leading cause of cancer death for women in Canada. Access to early breast cancer screening is limited in remote and low-income communities in Canada, as well as low and middle-income countries in the broader international community. Lack of accessible screening tools contributes to inequitable care and increased mortality rates. Microwave breast detection has shown promising results as a low-cost breast cancer screening modality. This work aims to design and develop a portable breast microwave detection device suitable for remote and low-income areas. The device consists of a cylindrical array of patch antennas and, through machine learning, will require no trained personnel to operate or obtain a preliminary diagnosis. Our initial work has monitored the coupling between adjacent antennas to determine the optimal number of patch antennas and experimentally determined the antenna cable time delay.

articleTitle: Wideband and Low-Loss Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna Fed by Printed Ridge-Gap Waveguide Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, A novel wideband magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna is introduced for 5G applications in millimeter-wave bands. This antenna supports a high radiation efficiency and stable gain characteristic. The designed antenna fed based on printed ridge-gap waveguide technology with low cross-polarization with basis on a complementary antenna structure. The proposed antenna exhibits a gain of more than 8.2 dBi in the whole operation frequency band.

articleTitle: Fabrication of an Embedded Multifunctional Structural Antenna for Spacecraft Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A design for a multifunctional structural embedded antenna was fabricated using novel materials. The system was built on top of a hybrid composite with an SU-8 polymer epoxy as the substrate and a copper patch antenna using adapted deposition methods. The antenna was designed to benefit spacecraft missions through reductions in size, risk, and overhead.

articleTitle: Approximate Solution of Large Linear Algebraic Systems Using Differential Equations
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Vector differential equations are constructed and then integrated numerically over an interval extended from a convenient starting value of the unknown to a value which gives the solution of the system of equations. The solution procedure allows to easily control and monitor the magnitude of the residual vector of the algebraic system at each step of the integration process. The method is flexible, permitting various intervening parameters to be changed wherever necessary in order to increase its efficiency. A smaller amount of computation is needed to obtain an approximate solution of very large linear systems as compared to existing methods. An electrostatic field model is suggested which could be useful for investigating techniques to further improve the efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Spectral Floquet analysis devoted to meta-surface applied for 5G and planned 6G antenna designs
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper provides a new mathematical Floquet modal analysis adequate to investigate the meta-surfaces for 5G and planned 6G antenna designs. A Fourier analysis is introduced to reduce the electromagnetic computation on a unit coupled cell (or on a unit block of coupled cells (finite coupled array)). This spectral formulation based on the discrete Floquet states permits the management of an infinite (or really large) antenna array with strong coupling interaction to several coupled sub-arrays employing a spatial period modulation phenomenon (in which the local period is modulated). The Moment method simplified by equivalent circuits MoM-GEC is applied as a numerical method to model the studied structures.

articleTitle: Truncated and Suspended Microstrip Patch Antennas Over an EBG Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: An extensive investigation has been performed with the objective of reducing the weight and profile of an EBG-backed microstrip antenna. Resulting from this study, two EBG-backed microstrip patch antennas, which are named "suspended" and "truncated," are introduced in this paper. Simulations are conducted to show that more than 70% reduction in weight and profile are achieved, while keeping the impressive antenna performance due to the presence of the EBG structure.

articleTitle: Modeling Normalized Radar Cross-Section of Oil-contaminated Sea Ice with Small Perturbation Method
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, we present a study of scattering from oil-contaminated sea ice. We utilized five dielectric mixture models to model clean and oil-contaminated sea ice with two types of oil products (crude oil and marine ship diesel) with 5% contamination by volume fraction. For the scattering approach, we utilized the Small Perturbation Method, SPM, and simulated the Normalized Radar Cross Section, NRCS, of clean and oil-contaminated sea ice at 5.5 GHz. Simulation results demonstrate that theoretically, although the difference is very small, the SPM method can be utilized for differentiating clean and contaminated sea ice and VV (Vertical-Vertical) polarization gives higher discrepancy than HH (Horizontal-Horizontal) polarization between clean and oil-contaminated sea ice.

articleTitle: Sea Ice Concentration from the RADARSAT Constellation Mission for Numerical Sea Ice Prediction
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this study, our technique for automated extraction of sea ice concentration from RADARSAT-2 data was adapted to the recently launched RADARSAT Constellation mission (RCM). Ice concentrations were derived from more than 2,600 RCM images acquired between August 1, 2020 and March 31, 2021. The retrieved ice concentrations were compared against the Canadian Ice Service (CIS) Image Analysis products. A very good agreement between RCM-derived and CIS Image Analysis ice concentrations was found with the root-mean square error of 2.2% and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.997. Our results suggest that automatically derived ice concentrations from RCM are well suited for further assimilation in sea ice numerical prediction systems such as Environment and Climate Change Canada Regional Ice-Ocean Prediction System.

articleTitle: Wideband and High-Gain Slot Antenna Using Self-Scalable Current Distribution and Multi-Mode Resonance
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: We present a compact, high-gain, and wideband coplanar waveguide (CPW)-fed slot antenna. This antenna makes use of self-scalable current distribution and multi-mode resonance (MMR) techniques to broaden the impedance matching condition and also to form a stable radiation pattern. It operates in K/Ka-band and covers a wide frequency range of 17-29.7GHz with 54% and 28% impedance and pattern bandwidth, respectively, showing a maximum realized gain of 9dBi. Owing to its simplicity, ease of integration, and high-gain radiation pattern, this antenna is a promising candidate for integrated circuit-antenna design.

articleTitle: A Quantitative Analysis of the Impact of Glass as a Phantom Shell Material in Breast Microwave Sensing
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Shell-based breast phantoms use shells to contain liquids that act as breast tissue surrogates by mimicking the dielectric properties of breast tissues. These phantoms are advantageous for their ease of use, robustness, and experimental utility. The use of liquids as the tissue mimicking material allows the user to create and readily modify liquid solutions to model the desired dielectric properties, the free positioning of tumour surrogates inside healthy tissues, and experimental reproducibility and transparency when 3D-printed plastic shells are used. The primary disadvantage of shell-based phantoms is their use of (typically low permittivity) shell materials to hold the tissue-mimicking liquids. This work investigates the impact of a 0.66 mm thick glass shell, used to contain a tumour-mimicking solution, on the measured S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> response in a pre-clinical breast microwave sensing system. A statistical analysis of the results obtained in this work indicate that the presence of the glass shell produces a response that cannot be detected by the imaging system, and therefore is suitable for use in shell-based phantoms.

articleTitle: 3-bit Anisotropic Metasurfaces with a Rotation of Meta-particles for Wideband RCS Reduction
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: 3-bit metasurfaces (MSs) made of meta-particles in the shape of a dumbbell with coding of the angle of inclination of the anisotropy axes from 0º to 180º with a discretion of 22.5º were investigated. The meta-particle anisotropy axes were oriented azimuthally or radially (in polar coordinate systems specified in the center of the modules). The modules provide cancellation of scattered fields of circular co-polarizations by no less than 10 dB in the band 8.4 to 19.2 GHz. MSs made of modules of the same or different types are investigated. Simulation at normal incidence showed that the RCS reduction of the MSs for linear co-polarizations is no less than 9-10 dB in the band 8.4 to 18.4 GHz. The backscattered field of circular co-polarization is practically absent. The deviations of the diffraction lobes from the reverse direction are from 17º to 65º at different frequencies and in different planes.

articleTitle: High gain and Wideband Antenna using a synthesized PRS layer for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband and high gain Fabry Perot Resonator Antenna (FPRA), with a single partially reflective surface (PRS) layer, that has a relatively high reflection coefficient magnitude, with a positive phase gradient, which resembles that of the optimum PRS over the frequency band of interest is proposed. This design achieved an impedance bandwidth of 22.73% (6.36 GHz) ranging from 24.8 GHz to 31.16 GHz, and the 3-dB gain bandwidth was 22.10 % (6.26 GHz) from 25.2 to 31.45 GHz, with a peak gain of 16.2 dB at 29 GHz. The simulated results showed important enhancements, justifying the feasibility of the proposed antenna as a high gain and wideband FP resonator antenna for Mm-Wave applications.

articleTitle: Data-adaptive filtering approach for microwave breast imaging: consistency of volunteer scans
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Microwave imaging (MI) is suited to monitoring breast health due to its safety and low cost. A microwave imaging transmission system (MITS) is being developed at the University of Calgary to measure and monitor the permittivity of tissue over time. This preliminary study presents an adaptive filtering technique to remove higher frequency artifacts, likely caused by incomplete contact between the skin and the antennas. This work investigates the impact of the filtering method on scans of two volunteers taken at different time points. As good contact between antennas and tissue is achieved for these scans, small changes are anticipated after application of the filtering strategy. Results show that the consistency of signals, permittivity estimates, and images over time is high, before and after filtering, for both volunteers. This preliminary study suggests that the filtering approach has potential for removing artifacts at higher frequencies, while preserving the integrity of clean signals.

articleTitle: Excessive Aperture Efficiency of Compact Antennas Demonstrated by Waveguides and Small Horns
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In modeling antennas using the aperture theory the peak gain occurs when the aperture amplitude and phase distributions are uniform, where the aperture efficiency becomes 100%. This is true when one uses the effective aperture of the antenna. In compact antennas the edge diffractions and current on outside walls of the antenna extend the aperture field well beyond the physical aperture of the antenna, and the effective aperture becomes much larger than the physical one. Thus, in using the physical aperture to calculate the aperture efficiency of the antenna, it exceeds 100%. This is demonstrated here by studying the aperture efficiencies of open-ended waveguides and small horns. Their field penetrations beyond their physical aperture are also investigated.

articleTitle: Development of extra low mass harmonic radar transponders
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: The current lightest available harmonic radar tags, with mass of a few milligrams, can only be carried by relatively large insects. However, small insects such as weevils and mosquitos are unable to sustain available tags. The former extensively infest food, and the latter kills nearly three million people and infects another 200 million or more every year. Two methods for reducing the tag’s mass and struggles of using these methods are presented here, followed by a review of the solutions. Retaining tag efficiency must be considered in every approach so as not to lose the detecting range because of impedance mismatch between the dipole and attached diode. These approaches include using a thinner wire and a short non-resonant dipole. The simulation was performed using Computer Simulation Technology (CST) software. Consequently, a wire tag lighter than 200-300 μg is expected, which has low mass for tracking smaller insects.

articleTitle: Compact Frequency Selective Surface Antenna for Grain Moisture Content Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel frequency selective surface (FSS) antenna for monitoring the moisture content (MC) in X-band (8–12 GHz). In the proposed sensor, the sample under test acts as the substrate of the antenna sandwiched between an array of square split ring resonators (SSRR) at the top plate and a ground plate at the bottom. The center frequency is chosen as 10 GHz. The width, length, and thickness of the FSS are 21 mm, 50 mm, and 0.017 mm, respectively. The compactness, sensitivity, and simplicity of the proposed antenna make it a suitable candidate as a portable microwave sensor for moisture content monitoring.

articleTitle: 3D Polarized Field-Forming for Mitigation of Angular Misalignment Problem in Microwave Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper addresses the angular misalignment problem in the far-field Microwave Power Transfer systems operating at 5.8GHz using the proposed 3D polarized field-forming technique. A 3D rotating E-field is generated by using a distributed antenna system to achieve this objective. The system is analyzed to understand the effect of 3D rotating E-field in comparison to the 2D E-field (circular polarization). The analytical results are verified using a commercial simulator and prove the potential of the proposed 3D polarized field-forming technique to achieve an orientation-insensitive MPT system to power a freely rotating receiver node.

articleTitle: Experiments with estimation of sea ice concentration using a convolutional neural network and microwave data
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Using an existing convolutional neural network (CNN) framework that uses both synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data and passive microwave data to learn sea ice concentration (SIC), we test the inclusion of different passive microwave channels and also perturbing the labels used in the loss function. Improved results are found if the low frequency channels from the passive microwave data are included. We also find perturbing the labels may be a reasonable approach to improved SIC estimation in marginal ice zones.

articleTitle: Ferrite Loaded Shielded Half Loop Antenna for Electromagnetic Imaging inside Metallic Chambers
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: With the goal of improving signal-to-noise ratio in stored-grain Electromagnetic Imaging, an electrically small Ferrite Loaded Shielded Half Loop Antenna (FLSHLA) in the 200-400 MHz band has been designed, simulated, fabricated, and tested. Using a scaled grain-bin EMI system, it is shown that loading a Shielded Half Loop Antenna (SHLA) with ferrite materials increases the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> by ~20 dB over previously used (non-loaded) SHLA. This signal improvement is achieved without the need of matching circuits which are often necessary in electrically small antennas.

articleTitle: A Circularly-Polarized Antenna for 5G Applications Fed by Printed Ridge-Gap Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, a multilayered circularly polarized (CP) antenna fed by a printed ridge-gap waveguide (PRGW) is presented. In the PRGW section, a 90-degree hybrid coupler is designed to provide a dual-mode generating CP feature at millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) bands. Then the coupler passes the signal from PRGW to the coaxial which plays an excitation role for the radiation section. The radiation section consists of two-layer of substrates and two square patches. The proposed antenna can cover a frequency bandwidth from 26.3-30 GHz (|S11 < -10 dB|) and it supports CP features in the frequency range from 27-30 GHz with an axial ratio (AR) less than 3-dB.

articleTitle: Tomographic Approach to Human Hydration Assessment: In Silico Proof-of-Concept
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Hydration is an important aspect of human health, with changes as little as 2% in body weight having measurable physiological effects. Standard microwave tomography techniques are applied in silico to realistic forearm models to detect changes in dielectric properties representative of water loss. Using a simple bulk properties metric, changes as small as 2% water content can be accurately tracked.

articleTitle: Grating Lobe Mitigation in Wide and Near Horizon Scanning Linear Arrays with One-Wavelength Element Spacing
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper addresses the grating lobe issue in linear, wide-angle scanning phased array antennas with one-wavelength element spacing by exciting two higher order modes in the element level. The antenna element is a dual–mode circular microstrip patch antenna operating at the TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">31</inf> modes with conical radiation patterns. By properly combining these modes, a radiation-matched element pattern, well suited for the wide scanning angles up to ±85°, is realized that can effectively reduce the grating lobes to well below -30 dB.

articleTitle: Frequency Scalability of Dual-polarized Flat-wire Open Loop Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This work investigates the frequency scalability of a dual-polarized flat-wire open loop antenna with wide bandwidth and low cross-polarization. Previously, we demonstrated the concept for an L-band design and in this work we extend the analysis to consider the performance of four frequency-scaled antennas operating in L, S, C and X-bands. Two types of scaling, namely, ideal scaling and quasi-ideal scaling, are investigated. The simulation results show that the flat-wire open loop antenna has excellent frequency scalability. and the ideal scaling does not affect the percentage impedance bandwidth and the radiation patterns of the antenna. The quasi-ideal scaling with unscaled substrate thickness, excitation port diameter and loop and ground structure wall thicknesses is also capable of preserving the attractive qualities of the antenna while allowing for easier fabrication.

articleTitle: Radar Antenna Gain Improvement Using 3D-Printed Dielectric Lens and Metamaterial-Inspired Superstrates
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, gain improvement methods based on lens and metamaterial inspired structures are investigated for the HB100 X-band radar. All proposed structures are implemented using low-cost and easy-to-fabricate 3D printing technology. The full-wave EM simulation shows gain improvement of 7.1 dB, 5.4 dB, and 5.5 dB using a hyperbolic lens, a hemispherical lens, and parallel dielectric plate, respectively, for both elevation and azimuth directions at 10.525 GHz.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Dual-Band Circular Patch Antenna Excited in Broadside TM11 & TM12 Modes
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: The inherent sidelobes in the antenna patterns have barred antenna designers from exploring the ability of the higher order broadside modes of circular microstrip patches for dual-band applications. Overcoming the sidelobe constraint, in this paper, a novel dual-band circular microstrip patch antenna excited in the dominant TM11 mode and higher order broadside TM12 mode operating at 0.9 GHz and 2.45 GHz, respectively, is presented. The advantage of the proposed antenna is that it is compact in size and free from sidelobes at both the bands.

articleTitle: Improvement of Phase Noise Characetristics of Reflective Type Push-Push Oscillator by Using Microstrip-Line Resonators
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In recent years, microwave and millimeter-wave frequency bands have been widely used with the development of mobile communication. However, in such a high frequency band, there are problems that the manufacturing cost of oscillators is high and the phase noise characteristic is not enough. Among high-frequency oscillators, a Push-Push oscillator is a harmonic oscillator that can be manufactured with low cost. In this study, an improvement method of the phase noise characteristics for the Push-Push oscillator is proposed. By using microstrip-line resonators coupled with the resonator used in the oscillator, the phase noise is improved by around 4 dB at 1-MHz offset frequency.

articleTitle: Temperature Sensing Using Wireless Passive Contactless Air-Filled Substrate-Integrated Waveguide (CLAF-SIW)
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, a high quality factor contactless air-filled substrate-integrated waveguide (CLAF-SIW) for temperature sensing is presented and experimentally tested. The resonant frequency of the CLAF-SIW sensor is determined by the dielectric constant of the electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) substrate and the dimensions of the structure where both parameters are temperature-dependent. As a result, the resonant frequency of the CLAF-SIW sensor changes with temperature. The temperature sensing behaviour of the structure and its linearity and repeatability was verified by experiments. A sensitivity of 311.5 kHz/°C was achieved and its linearity shows that the sensor is a viable candidate for wireless passive temperature sensing.

articleTitle: Alternate Minimizations for an Approximate Solution of General Systems of Linear Algebraic Equations
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A special kind of a functional associated with a general linear system of equations, which allows not only to minimize the value of the functional but also the distance to the solution point, is used for an efficient computation of an approximate solution of the system. A formula is derived for the minimization of the distance to the solution point. The two types of minimization are applied alternately to approach the solution. This simple method gives satisfactory results even for poorly conditioned systems.

Author Keywords: approximate solution of linear algebraic systems

articleTitle: Overview of Nano-Sphere and Nano-Rod Geometries for Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance Biosensing
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance (LSPR) biosensors utilize the extinction spectra resulting from the interaction between incident light photons and metallic Nano-Particles (NP) to study the variation in the surrounding medium Refractive Index (RI). In this paper, we will discuss the response of the LSPR extinction spectra to the nano-sphere and nano-rod NP geometries of differing dimensions. We will also discuss the response of the LSPR extinction spectra to variations in the Refraction Index (RI) of the medium surrounding the metallic NP. Also, we will explain the sensitivity, Detection Accuracy (DA) and Figure of Merit (FoM) performance parameters for LSPR sensors. We will also compare the sphere and Rod NP geometries.

articleTitle: Hertzian Magnetic Dipoles Model of a Quasi-isotropic radiation microstrip patch based Antenna-in-Package
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: The Internet of Things applications require small wireless sensors with quasi isotropic radiation, so that their placement is orientation insensitive. This paper shows the design steps for a microstrip patch based quasi-isotropic Antenna-in-Package (AiP). The structure proposed is a hollow cube with six microstrip patch radiators, one on each of its faces. The cubes internal walls are metallized to not only act as ground planes for the microstrip patch antennas, but also provide the necessary shielding between the radiators and the future embedded electronics. Thus, the problem in hand is to find the optimal phases to be applied to each patch so that when all six are activated simultaneously, the obtained radiation pattern is quasi-isotropic. Given the complexity of the structure, a simplified model of Hertzian magnetic dipoles was used to determine the phase each patch was to be excited to achieve the closest to an isotropic radiator as possible. A measured gain variation of 6.5 dB has been achieved for the entire 3D sphere after fabrication of a prototype.

articleTitle: Using Lossy Green’s Functions to Improve Back-Propagated Reconstructions of Material Interfaces inside Resonant Enclosures
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Successful grain bin Electromagnetic Imaging (EMI) requires knowledge of the grain/air interface. With the goal of determining an arbitrary grain/air material interface, we present a 2-D synthetic model and use back-propagation with a numerical Green’s function for the metallic-walled bin. Although the bin is partially filled with both air and grain, inside such metallic chambers we show that back-propagation can recreate the grain/air interface when the background Green’s function is selected to be the one associated with a bin full of grain (not air).

articleTitle: A Novel Microstrip Line Based Leaky Wave Antenna using Capacitive Loading
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A novel MLWA with integrated varactor diodes is presented in this work. The design relies on integrated FPMS unit cells that can modulate the substrate properties of the antenna to provide the required radiation characteristics. The phase constant of the wave along the antenna length is varied in a controlled fashion by virtue of these unit cells to steer the maximum of the beam. At 2 GHz, and using Duroid 5880 as the substrate, the antenna provides a simulated gain of 11 dBi with beam scanning in the backward direction. A good correlation can be observed between the theory and simulations that provides confidence on this proof-of-concept design. With high gain and acceptable impedance matching, this design provides a platform for investigation of FPMS based reconfigurable antenna elements.

articleTitle: A Compact Beam-Steerable Integrated Reflectarray Antenna for LEO Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, a beam-steerable metamaterial reflectarray antenna is proposed for low earth orbiting communication satellite applications. The feed holder stand was replaced by a flexible PF-4 foam. As a result, the whole antenna has an integrated planar structure and a continuous beam switching with 30-degree freedom was achieved. The distance between feed and the reflectarray plate is only 0.36 λc, the wavelength at 27 GHz. Furthermore, the 7×7 metamaterial antenna array demonstrated a stable maximum gain higher than 12 dB over a wide bandwidth from 23.5 GHz to 30.5 GHz.

articleTitle: A Triangularly Packed Planar Array of Dual-polarized L-band Flat-wire Open Loop Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Previously, we proposed an L-band dual-polarized flat wire open loop antenna with wide bandwidth and low cross-polarization. In this work, we extend our study to its array form to improve the antenna gain. A triangular lattice is adopted to minimize the inter-element spacing and eliminate grating lobes. The simulation results show that a gain improvement of 5.82 dB can be achieved using a 4-element array while maintaining other attractive properties of the antenna. Due to the metallic ground plane side walls, despite of dense packing, the mutual coupling among elements is low.

articleTitle: Volatility Modeling for Ocean Significant Wave Height Estimation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In a previous paper by the same authors in the current conference series [1], an interesting relation was derived which showed that the significant wave height H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> is linearly proportional to the standard deviation of the received time series from a monostatic HF radar. In the current paper we use this relation along with methods from the field of volatility modeling, which is often used in financial mathematics, to provide accurate estimates of significant wave height. We demonstrate on field data from Argentia, Newfoundland, Canada that the use of such methods gives slightly more accurate H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> estimates than using a simple windowed variance calculation.

articleTitle: Towards Calibration of Uncooperative Electromagnetic Imaging Systems using CycleGANs
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: An uncooperative electromagnetic inversion system, e.g., a grain storage bin, makes it difficult to calibrate the numerical and physical system models. In this work, we investigate the idea of training a CycleGAN to convert experimentally collected S-parameter data into calibrated field data suitable for subsequent electromagnetic inversion. A simple proof of concept, applied to synthetically generated "experimental" data, is implemented, trained, and evaluated. Results demonstrate the potential for CycleGANs to play an important role in electromagnetic imaging.

articleTitle: Multiband RF Front-End in LTCC for Avionic Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A receiver architecture relying on special RF front-end filtering to separate different services is proposed in which a dual band-pass filter and a dual band coupler are required enabling a multi-standard multi-service direct conversion receiver covering the VHF and UHF avionic services. RF front-end integration is fabricated in low temperature co- fired ceramic (LTCC) technology using a lumped element approach. The overall size of the integration is 59mm×38mm×2.2mm.

articleTitle: Optimization of HF Receiving Antenna with Horizontal Polarization based on ITU Noise Model
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: An optimization process for the horizontally polarized HF-band receive antenna based on an extended concept of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) noise model "ITU-R P.372-14 on radio noise" is presented. Considering the ambient noise (or sky noise), a receiving antenna has been optimized based on the concept of equivalent antenna system noise figure. Furthermore, the ambient noise is evaluated with the optimized antenna and the results are compared with the reference noise curves.

articleTitle: Design of a SIW Variable Phase Shifter for Beamforming Antenna Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: The main objective of this article is to design a controllable broadband phase-shifter based on the Integrated Substrate Waveguide (SIW) technique using PIN diodes buried in the substrate to switch between ON and OFF states. The proposed geometry is designed and optimized by numerical EM simulator (HFSS). The proposed phase shifter is designed to operate across a large bandwidth ranging from 8 GHz to 12GHz. The simulation results show that a maximum differential phase of 136 deg was achieved with acceptable return loss and insertion loss.

articleTitle: Estimation of Monostatic Radar Cross Section of Chaff Particles Using the Sequential Loading Method
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This study presents an efficient and reliable approach to rapidly estimate the scattering properties of chaff particles. This approach adopts the sequential loading method (SLM) which is an iterative post-processing technique that is capable of predicting the new solution of different chaff particles without having to reuse any expensive computational electromagnetic (CEM) tools. The SLM operates solely on the initial solution of a single chaff particle for which the admittance matrix is previously calculated, only once, via the moment method. The calculation of the spatially averaged radar cross section (RCS) of the chaff particles contained in the RR-129 cartridge is successfully obtained by including both reradiation and conductive power losses. Also, a comparison between the estimated results and measured ones is attempted for a single chaff particle of length 5.08 cm.

articleTitle: TDR-Based Fault Detection in Grounding Electrodes Using a Rod Insertion Method
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper describes a TDR-based technique for vertical grounding electrode fault diagnostics using a rod insertion method. In this technique, a supporting rod is employed to transmit a TEM wave. The delay of reflected propagating wave for various length of the rod is analyzed to identify the corroded damaged area on the grounding electrode. Full wave simulations show that the approach is capable of detecting faults to an accuracy of cm with a system bandwidth of 300 MHz.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network for the First Filter Design Stage using the Reflected Group Delay Method
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents an artificial neural network model for predicting the geometric parameters of a filter based on input filter design parameters. This model is applied to the first design stage of the reflected group delay method, which consists of determining the geometric parameters of the first resonator of a filter. Parameter extraction is performed on EM simulation results of a single resonator to generate the data required to train the model, which converges with no overfitting. The model is successfully used to predict the geometric parameters of a microstrip resonator.

articleTitle: Compact Design of Hybrid-Coupled Filter Module (HCFM) Using Inter-Resonator Couplings
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: The hybrid-coupled filter module (HCFM) multiplexers are widely used as RF combiners in wireless and satellite communication systems. A conventional HCFM consists of two complete 3dB hybrid couplers. In this paper, compact designs of HCFM are presented. The inter-resonator coupling between two filters is used to replace one of the branches in a 3dB hybrid coupler, resulting in significant size reduction. As demonstrated using design examples implemented in different technologies, including rectangular waveguide and substrate integrated waveguide (SIW), the proposed compact structure preserves the responses of a conventional design. EM simulations and/or measurements results are presented to validate the design concept. Moreover, using tuning elements, such as tuning screws or varactor diodes, tunable designs can be realized.

articleTitle: mmWave Propagation Prediction using Hardware- Accelerated Monte Carlo Path Tracing
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: We have developed a hardware-accelerated Monte Carlo path tracing tool based upon a novel mmWave propagation prediction model. Much faster than conventional tools, it is designed to meet the needs of large-scale coverage and interference studies. The results of initial validation against conventional ray- tracing simulations and measurements in an indoor office environment at 60 GHz demonstrate the merit of the approach. Overall, prediction accuracy was comparable between the two approaches in this scenario, while Monte Carlo path tracing was more than an order of magnitude faster. With further validation and suitable building and terrain data, this method should also be suitable for outdoor and mixed environments.

articleTitle: A wavelet-based contrast source inversion method
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A wavelet transform is applied to the contrast source inversion (CSI) method to tackle the highly nonlinear inverse scattering problem. The latter is about retrieving the contrast or permittivity and conductivity of the unknown scattering object from measured electromagnetic field data. A multi-scale wavelet-based method is proposed due to the multi-resolution property of the wavelet decomposition.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of K-Band Sequentially Rotated Wideband Circularly Polarized Phased Arrays using Different Array Lattices
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: This paper presents a performance comparison of a K-band wideband sequentially rotated circularly polarized phased array aperture utilizing three different array lattices – triangular, square and hexagonal. These array lattices were assessed for their circular polarization and radiation performances. The square lattice was found to be superior compared to its triangular and hexagonal counterparts.

articleTitle: Scattered field data collection in multi-static/ multi-frequency radar imaging
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this contribution, the problem to collect the scattered field data in multi-static and multi-frequency configuration in the framework of radar imaging problem is addressed.

articleTitle: Using Selected Rates of Residual Vector Decrease for Solving Iteratively Large Linear Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Cycles of iteration with an imposed rate of decrease of the residual vector at the beginning of each cycle are used to derive an approximate solution of linear systems of algebraic equations. When the rate of decrease of the residual vector deteriorates significantly a new cycle of iteration is performed with the starting value of the unknown being the value computed in the preceding cycle. The latter is improved by bringing it as close as possible to the exact solution of the system by applying a formula derived in a previous work. The method is straightforward and of high efficiency for computing an approximate solution of large systems.

Author Keywords: approximate iterative solution of linear algebraic systems

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Antenna based on Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons using Artificial Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, a circularly polarized highly efficient broadside antenna based on spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) using polarization dependent artificial ground plane (AGP) is proposed. Printed monopole is used to excite even mode of SSPPs in 45° rotated corrugated strip relative to ground plane. The field from the resonating even mode and reflected field from the polarization dependent artificial ground plane contribute for circular polarization in broadside direction. The proposed antenna offers 10-dB input impedance bandwidth and 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) of 15.3% and 11.7% (at 3.42 GHz center frequency) in broadside direction with right hand circular polarization (RHCP), respectively. The minimum axial ratio achieved is 0.39 dB. The total efficiency remains above 92.4% over 3-dB ARBW, while maximum total efficiency achieved is 98.4%. The proposed antenna provides very low cross polar component with maximum gain value of 7.17 dBic in broadside direction.

articleTitle: Utilizing the Ferromagnetic Battery of Capsule Endoscopes for Static Magnetic Localization
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Static magnetic localization of capsule endoscopes is an established research area but the ferromagnetic battery shell of capsule endoscopes has not been investigated so far. Therefore, in this study, the batteries were enclosed by a ring magnet, suitable for a commercial capsule, and the magnetization effect of the ferromagnetic battery shell was evaluated. The magnet and the batteries were moved along the x-axis while the position and orientation errors were determined to investigate if the dipole model applies for the setup. The achieved mean position and orientation errors were below 1 mm and 0.1°, respectively. It was concluded that the built-in batteries can advantageously increase the magnetic flux density up to 25 %, depending on the magnetization direction of a ring magnet and the dipole model applies even with the enclosed batteries.

articleTitle: A Microstrip Patch Antenna Over an EBG Ground Plane and Covered with Partially Reflecting Surface
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Performance of a microstrip patch antenna over a high impedance electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structure, covered by a dielectric surface is investigated. While running a study on the effect of design parameters on the antenna performance, an impressive directivity improvement has been obtained.

articleTitle: Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna using Barium Strontium Titanate Sol-Gel Adhesive
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A Barium Strontium Titanate (BST) Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna (RDRA) was constructed on a FR4 Printed Circuit Board (PCB). The RDRA was innovatively glued to the PCB using dried sol-gel BST composite as opposed to epoxy, which has not been done before. Adhesion pull tests indicated that an average load of 161 grams can be applied before separation of RDRA and PCB occurs. The RDRA antenna gain was 3.6 dB for the RDRA in TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1δ1</inf> mode at 10.1 GHz.

articleTitle: Effect of Enclosure on Deep Brain Ablation Using Time-Reversing Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: The capability of metasurfaces to shape the wavefront is used to provide the desired outgoing fields in focusing fields on deep-seated brain target. The wavefront is obtained via time-reversal focusing technique and the corresponding metasurface is designed by generalized sheet transition condition (GSTC) method. Also Perfect Electric Conductor (PEC) walls are used to enhance the focusing resolution. Simulation results show acceptable focusing in terms of resolution and hot spots.

articleTitle: A Performance Comparison of Three Topologies of Circular Loop Antennas Transmitting Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A preliminary comparative study of wireless power transfer systems composed of three different topologies of the transmitting loops is addressed in this paper. The key feature of this study is to demonstrate that a dual transmitter topology provides better performance than a single transmitter topology from the power transfer efficiency point of view. The frequency of the proposed structures can be adjusted by means of scaling its dimensions and it can be used for electric vehicle wireless charging and powering medical implants.

articleTitle: Backscattering Cancellation of Blocks of Anisotropic 2-Bit Meta-Coatings
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Cancellation of the backscattering patterns (BSPs) of two main blocks of anisotropic 2-bit thin meta-coatings (MC) is numerically and experimentally investigated. Good matching of the simulation and measurement results of BSP in the area of central lobes for different planes and polarizations of irradiation is shown. In the principal planes, the central lobes of the BSP for co- and cross-polarizations are suppressed by 10-25 dB. The BSP in the sector of angles about ±40° is lower than that of the reference. In the diagonal plane, the expansion (approximately two times) of the BSP central lobe for co-polarizations and the bifurcation of this lobe for cross-polarizations (with a deep cancellation of up to 35 dB at normal incidence) are noted.

articleTitle: Towards the Shape Synthesis of Circularly-Polarized Dielectric Resonator Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: We describe how characteristic mode based objective functions can be constructed to apply an earlier shape synthesis method for dielectric resonator antennas (DRA) to the case where a circularly-polarized broadside pattern is required using a single feed, even without reflectional symmetry.

articleTitle: Dynamic-Range Improvement of Energy Harvesting Circuit for Indoor Environment Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, power detector for RF energy harvesting for indoor application is presented at 2.45 GHz. This designed circuit is intended to improve dynamic range, with a dynamic range of (45) dBm for indoor application. A series array of diodes is used to rectify the DC output, and a microstrip transmission line is used to match the circuit to a 50 Ω input impedance. The measured DC output voltage is 8.6 V, and the working range is (-20 to 25)dBm. The simulated and measured results showed a good linearity with acceptable efficiency and a wide dynamic range. The proposed circuit is validated by experimental results at indoor environments.

articleTitle: Adjustable Input Impedance Dipole
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this paper, a novel dipole design with an adjustable input impedance is presented. The proposed dipole is designed to have additional arms attached at the edges of the feeding gap for the purpose of controlling the input impedance. Varying the dimensions of the two arms enables the tuning of the input impedance. This design is highly suitable for systems where the input impedance of the antenna needs to be directly matched to the input impedance of a receiving circuit. The proposed antenna eliminates the need for matching circuits which may deteriorate the efficiency of the entire system.

Author Keywords: inductive input impedance and capacitive input impedance

articleTitle: Beam Focusing by using Scattering From Drones
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Beam focusing is commonly done by using phased arrays. However, the size of a phased array typically increases as the frequency is lowered, making beamforming at lower frequencies more difficult to achieve. For example, at 30 MHz, the wavelength is about 10 meters, making the needed element separation in the range of 5–10 meters. Such a large array would be difficult to easily make in a mobile or airborne form. One possible solution is to use drones as the radiating elements, since it is easy to position them almost arbitrarily in space. Such a drone-based array could be useful in certain applications. For example, communications between a transmitter and a remote receiver might be blocked, so that there is no direct line of sight between the transmitter and the receiver. This might happen, for example, if the transmitter is located inside of a forest or mountainous region. In this case the drone swarm could be used as a relay between the transmitter and receiver, flying at a sufficient altitude to overcome the blockage. (The transceiver that is located inside the forest or mountainous region is being thought of as the transmitter for convenience.)

articleTitle: Wideband Corporate Center-fed Antenna for 79GHz Automotive Radar Application
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A wideband microstrip corporate center-fed antenna is developed for automotive radar application (79 GHz). The power tapering is applied to achieve desired Side Lobe Level (SLL). A microstrip to microstrip transition from top side to the back side of the board is also designed for interconnecting this antenna and active parts on the back side of the board. The overall antenna and transition are simulated.

articleTitle: TX-to-RX Leakage Canceler for IoT RFID Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: The performance of the ultra-high frequency (UHF) radio frequency identification (RFID) systems are usually degraded by inadequate transmitter-to-receiver (TX-to-RX) isolation. In order to tackle this problem, in this paper a broadband leakage canceler is presented. The proposed canceler utilizes a two-stage lumped element Wilkinson power divider and a direct leaky coupling circuit (DLCC) in order to provide a high isolation between the TX and RX paths. The measured results for the implemented leakage canceler are in fine agreement with the simulation results. The fabricated leakage canceler occupies only 53×30×0.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> while providing an isolation better than -40 dB in the UHF RFID frequency band of 0.812-0.965 GHz.

articleTitle: A New Closed-Form Approach (Equation) for Accurately Predicting the Efficiency of Square Patch Planar Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Patch antenna is one of the most common type of antenna design due to its simplicity of orientation, dimension, configuration, and ease of implementation over a vast and variety of materials: such as fabrics to printed circuit boards. This work discovers and shows how to quickly predict the efficiency of a simple patch without the need for expensive software and/or hardware using a novel equation that relates the loss tangent, dielectric constant, and substrate height to patch efficiency. This first of a kind equation is used for assessing whether the efficiency of the patch is suitable enough for use on said intended exotic material substrate that have height of 62 mils or less (which is respectfully suitable for most applications). The simple closed form equation can predict efficiency with high accuracy. Discrepancies between quick ADS electromagnetic (EM) simulations and predictions were less than 5%-7% error for various materials (with height ≤ 62 mils) at frequencies ranging from 2.5 GHz - 10 GHz.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Multifunctional Terahertz Holographic Metasurface using CMOS Chip Tiling
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: In this article, we exploit electromagnetic-circuit co-design approach to demonstrate a digitally reconfigurable metasurface at 0.3 THz. Realized on an industry standard 65-nm CMOS process, each metasurface CMOS chip consists 12×12 array of reconfigurable split-ring unit cells. Reconfiguration of each unit cell happens through EM-circuit co-designed CMOS transistor switches. Each unit-cell is individually addressable and controllable with on-chip high-speed digital back-end. Scalability of this approach is demonstrated by tiling such CMOS chips to form a larger aperture of 2×2 array. We experimentally demonstrate multi-functional applications namely, arbitrary amplitude and phase control, high-speed beam modulation with switching ON/OFF ratio of ~25 dB at a maximum clock speed of 5 GHz, beamforming capability of ± 30°, and spatial wavefront manipulation using binary-amplitude-only holography technique at 0.3 THz. Each metasurface consumes a total DC power of (240 µW) consumption and operates at 1.2V.

articleTitle: Open Source Visualization for Radar Altimetry Waveforms
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: Radar altimetry is a valuable tool for monitoring topographic changes in Earth’s polar regions. An important part of these altimetry data sets is the waveforms that are received and recorded by the radar. These waveforms are processed to create surface-height data products, but also contain information about the scattering surface and near-subsurface. However, there is currently not open-source software available for visualizing these radar altimetry waveforms in an efficient and reproducible workflow. This paper presents OpenWaveforms, a software application that is in development that will make lower-level radar altimetry data products more accessible and user-friendly for researchers. The current state of the software is shown, along with the next steps planned for the software and the goals for the finished application.

articleTitle: Study of a SAR Mission Onboard a 12U CubeSat using the Reflectarray Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A synthetic aperture radar antenna using the reflectarray concept is proposed for a 12U CubeSat. Based on a 5-panel antenna configuration allowed by the size of the CubeSat and the Canisterized Satellite Dispenser, a feed patch array is proposed for the reflectarray illumination. Simulated patterns of the whole dual-polarized Ku-band antenna indicate that the performance of the proposed antenna would allow imaging with a 50m x 50m spatial resolution.

articleTitle: A Miniaturizied Quasi-Yagi Antenna with Double Dog-bone Driver
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A miniaturized quasi-Yagi antenna is proposed. The structure of the antenna has a simple feeding mechanism consist of microstrip line and transmission line. Half of the driver is printed on the opposite side of the substrate to achieve stable radiation pattern. Double dog-bone driver and slotted ground structure with circular patches is utilized for the antenna miniaturization. Size of the miniaturizied antenna is 0.3λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>× 0.3λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>. The antenna has achieved |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| ≤ −10 dB between 2.35-2.5 GHz in the simulation, and 2.35-2.7 GHz in the measurement. The antenna shows high gain of 5-5.5 dBi, efficiency of over 90% and end-fire radiation pattern in operating frequency band. The proposed antenna is good candidate for wireless communication and radar systems.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Coplanar Slotted SIW Antenna Array for Fixed Frequency Beam Scanning Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics (ANTEM)
abstract: A new solution for reconfigurable antennas based on the substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology is presented in this paper. The structure is designed to operate at 25 GHz for beam-scanning applications.
